reason: Confusing scene with a forced word: 'The water looked big and shy, hiding behind the pool wall', and he climbs 'out' before ever getting in.
Time concepts contradict and threads tangle: Grandma says the puppy book comes 'Tomorrow, when we come back' but Henry gets it later the same day.
Muddled time definitions and dialogue: Mom asks then answers herself, 'Yesterday was the day before now... It is gone now', and 'Today, we read now'.
Abstract, jumpy ending: 'Stella was so lucky. One little sentence had started three games.'
Confusing score story for age 3: 'The game ended. Blue had three. Red had three again.' after blue led 3-2 with no red goal shown.
Confusing categories: 'She found a soft toy bear. She put it in the animal pile' in a toys-vs-animals sort.
Tangled setting: at the bus stop, yet 'Brooklyn picked it off the hook' by the door, plus the random 'I dream of dogs.'
Rambling plot (ball, teddy, cocoa, an unsung 'clean-up song', wagon) and an unsupervised climb 'up, up, up' to the top shelf.
Unclear plot: 'The shelf looked too high. Layla touched the jar' and the lid pops off by itself, with 'Two little openings took in the yummy smell.'
Overlong, and the ending muddles game cups with drink cups: 'Audrey passed the cups around... "I win this time!"' and a 'winner list.'
Mixed message: right after 'Charlie reached out and grabbed it,' the coach gives him a star sticker.
Confusing setup: cousin in a lifeguard 'high chair' at a green backyard pool, 'I need help' only to get a ball.
Abstract borrowing talk and unfamiliar words: 'due date', 'bookmobile', 'Then it is empty?'
Unsafe near flames: after the diyas are lit, 'Eleanor touched the cool clay on the outside only' is shown as fine.
Confusing for a child: babies come from a '"Baby store!"' and Logan tells a stranger's baby '"New baby, you can come home now."'
Off-topic cause-and-effect detour that states an abstract idea: 'One thing made another thing happen!' It also runs long for age 3.
Nobody corrects the child for pouring water on the floor, and she asks to do it again: 'She poured her cup of water onto the floor. Splash!' ... 'Splash again?'
Tangled setting, with a TV basketball game at an ice rink plus skaters: 'On the ice, a skater fell down. A fresh pile of snow sprayed up from her blades.'
A 3-year-old writing a sentence and learning word spacing is too advanced: 'In English, we put a space between one word and the next. The spaces help my eyes stop and go.'
Shirt-colour team mix-up is too tangled for age 3: '"Sam, I am not late, I forgot my shirt," Sam said,' then an own goal and a shirt swap.
Muddled time talk left unresolved: 'We came to this store tomorrow' then 'We came yesterday.'
Confusing premise and unknown word: 'Clara got to school in the dark... It is still night,' plus 'the radiator was hot.'
Clock-reading lecture beyond age 4: 'The big hand pointed to the twelve. The little hand pointed to the nine.'
Grabbing shown as fine: 'Max took the ball and ran off with it' then 'Thank you, Sam!' as the model of thanks.
Counting story miscounts and confuses: four beans plus two counted as 'Four, five, six, seven. Seven!'
Confusing senses logic ('You used your eyes to see' said when the doctor looks in Owen's mouth) and a plot that drifts from doctor to yard across 11 paragraphs.
Muddled time talk and forced words: 'Cow, I see Ben today', 'in a small mouth voice', 'Today is the day after yesterday', across 16 paragraphs.
Lecture-like chain of definitions: 'Today is the day happening right now.' 'Now is this minute.' 'Yesterday is the day that is done.'
Confusing actions and forced words: 'He gave her his one free hand. She laughed and put it on her ear.' and 'He looked at the wild steam.'
Plot contradicts itself: she counts 'three' aloud, then 'You skipped three, Riley,' and the egg 'got dry and cozy' under a blanket.
Confusing abstract reasoning: 'The blue crayon made her sun shine on the paper. One thing helped the other thing.'

Hockey penalty rules are beyond a 4-year-old: "A skater hit the puck with his stick too high" and "He makes the rules work!"; also a muddled line: "He asked Mom to color a referee... He drew the striped shirt".
Confusing plot: "Two grandmas, two grandpas, all with closed eyes. He counted them. One, two, two again." when only one of each is present, and bread becomes "soup time".
Forced, nonsensical required words: "That is my soup day beanbag... Mama sewed it from soup beans" and "woke up from being asleep"; the plot wanders.
Confusing count in a counting story: 'He picked up all ten of his hands' worth, one, two, three, four, five', plus the odd phrase 'bed toy'.
Unsafe climbing left uncorrected: 'She reached up high on the shelf... Lucy stepped on it... Then the stool tipped.' with no adult response, plus a tangled plot.
Abstract time reasoning: 'Was now this minute? ... Now meant right this minute, the very moment he was in.'
Muddled timeline undermines the time concept: 'Yesterday her moon picture had been all wet too. Today it hung on the wall, dry and shiny.'
Unsafe act shown as fine: 'Ben put bread in the toaster. He got it out with a fork.'
Dictionary-style line 'Clapping along to the beat means clapping at the same time as the beat of the music.' plus a rushed, long-sentence final paragraph.
Disjointed plot hopping from box to pillows to fire truck to soup, with confusing lines like 'Her spoon went fast when the soup was just right.'
Confusing opposites game: 'She said "hot" for the sun, but Sam said "cold."' counts a right answer as wrong, and 'Opposites are two different words' is abstract.
Plot doesn't hold together: Audrey practices K for her name, then 'She wrote A, U, D, and then a big, happy K.'
Confusing plot: he is told to bring the book back next week, then right away 'He dropped it in the slot.'
Confusing sorting logic: 'Bunny had fur. Socks were soft too! She laughed at her own silly mix-up and moved the sock to the shirt and the hat.'
Unexplained death theme for a 3-4-year-old: 'Ivy sat on the soft grass at the cemetery... near Grandpa Joe's stone.'
Confusing forced lines: 'He drew a plane on the paper with one' and 'They were the last ones in the box, but not too late to get them.'
Confusing plot: school rest time where 'It is dark outside. It is still night' and 'The moon was up', then 'Morning now' when the light comes on.
Unsafe behaviour left as fine: a 3-year-old 'ran out the door fast' to the park by a pond and 'ran back home' with no grown-up.
Mouthing a sticker played for laughs: 'Ivy put it on her tongue and tasted the shiny paper... Everyone laughed.'
Shelving concept too advanced and plot muddled: 'See this little label on the spine?' then Luke 'put it back in its spot. Then he took it to the desk.'
Confusing logic for a 3-year-old: 'That is not a fish... It is a toy' then the meat case ('Look, fish... And look, cow meat') and 'Fish can't be animals!'.
Contradictory time lesson: Dad says 'Good morning?... Now it is a new part of the day,' yet the story ends 'Good morning, birds!' unresolved.
Adult definition and confusing opening: 'Retracing your steps means going back to each place you went, in order' and 'But bear's other foot was empty.'
Unfocused, with forced and random details: 'Daddy did say', 'Outside the sky looked stormy and gray', 'saw her loose tooth wiggle in the mirror'.
Tangled plot with a forced, confusing line: 'It was the teacher’s baby, and it came on the last day of the week.' Also abstract: 'Where do babies go when they sleep?'
Confusing jump: 'He picked up the curvy letters and made a pile.' No letter cards are ever shown, and the pet turtle at 'writing club' is a random detail.
Confusing plot: 'The toy box got full and full. Then the box was empty. Sam had put everything away.'
Muddled plot and nonsensical required word: 'You found my answer!' and a hot pie 'near the oven area' in a store.
Confusing ending: Max says 'My turn now' then 'You can have them both', and grabbing is never addressed.
Confusing reasoning: 'Because his head was attached to his head! If he sat like a statue, his head would not move at all.'
Tangled counting logic: 'So there was no chair left for the spoon cup' and a nonsensical 'string of napkins' make it hard to follow.
Long flashback and an abstract generalization: 'Small toys always seemed to roll or slide under things and hide.'
Muddled pretend play: 'Tom's face looked sad and hard' and the bear suddenly becomes 'The baby fish fell asleep.'
Nonsensical cause and random ending: 'Sorry,' said Violet, 'I zipped too fast.' after the girl falls.
Reversed-order reading is hard for a 3-year-old to follow: 'The dog barked before he woke up.'
Tangled plot with shifting problems (apple grab, then 'He had a small bread roll to share. Avery broke it and gave him half.', then 'the pillow aisle') that is hard to follow.
Confusing who cheers for whom: 'But no one else clapped... Dad was clapping for the other team!' then 'their team scored again'.
Muddles the time concept it teaches ('Is it tomorrow now?' 'Yes,' said Mom) and uses past-perfect flashback ('had wanted to fly a kite') plus 'shy of the big kite'.
Confusing whose birthday it is: Mia says 'Today I am four. It is my birthday.' but the cake and candles are for Hunter.
Tangled time plot with confusing lines: 'Today is tomorrow now.' plus the bus boy and 'In the bus ride home'.
Long and relies on unfamiliar ideas: 'Then Miss Ada used the studio's warm press.' plus a hot-car melting chain.
